title: Understanding the Utility-First Concept
ques: Explain the core philosophy of **Utility-First CSS** in Tailwind CSS compared to traditional semantic CSS. Provide an HTML snippet for a stylized alert banner using Tailwind utility classes.

answer.content: A new software update is available! Check your system preferences.

explanation: Utility-first CSS prioritizes composing interfaces directly in HTML using atomic single-purpose utility classes. This eliminates naming overhead, prevents CSS file bloat, and provides visual consistency.

title: Pseudo-Class Modifiers: Hover, Focus, and Active
ques: Demonstrate the use of state modifiers (`hover:`, `focus:`, and `active:`) in Tailwind by writing an interactive primary call-to-action button.

answer.content:
<button class="px-5 py-2.5 text-white font-semibold bg-indigo-600 rounded-lg shadow-md transition-all duration-200 hover:bg-indigo-700 hover:shadow-lg focus:outline-none focus:ring-4 focus:ring-indigo-300 active:scale-95">
  Get Started
</button>

explanation: State modifiers in Tailwind prepend state names before utility classes, allowing seamless inline styling for interactive pseudoclasses like hover, focus rings, and active button depressions.

title: Dark Mode Configuration and Styling
ques: Explain the two dark mode strategies in Tailwind (`media` vs `class`). Write a card component using `dark:` variant utilities that automatically adapts to dark themes.

answer.content:
Dark Mode Support

Using the dark class strategy, Tailwind checks the presence of a 'dark' class on the root html element to seamlessly invert theme colors.

explanation: Using the `class` dark mode strategy allows toggling a `.dark` class on the `<html>` root via JavaScript, triggering all `dark:` utility variants across the entire page.
